steps.content: The lights in the interrogation room are turned off. Someone is murmuring in the darkness.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world. You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you to the light. Where there is light, there you shall be.
You find this poem oddly familiar.
When you walk in, Oak Casket nods to greet you.
She sits in a relaxed posture in the interrogation chair, gently gazing at you as though she is the one in control of the interrogation room.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You're here.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: What do you seek from me this time?
Oak Casket's tone is calm and unperturbed, yet you can feel a sense of distance.
Your support, or something along the lines.

You gently flip open the folder, revealing several pictures of the ruined Romanesque Hall after the explosion of the Black Ring. You slide it forward, but Oak Casket only glances at it before returning her gaze to you.
The Rustfire crisis in West District is over now. The people of West District and the Eastside City Council hope to start the reconstruction of Syndicate as soon as possible.

We also deeply regret the severe damage the Romanesque Hall suffered during the battle, but we've already planned to repair it, and... construct a monument for those who lost their lives in the disaster.
Now, we need someone who has the required knowledge to assist us in our work.
We believe there aren't any other better candidates than you.
You thought Oak Casket would agree to repair the hall and the surrounding stelae despite her look of disdain. But to your surprise, Oak Casket voices her refusal.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Regretfully, there isn't much I can do.
But... no one knows the number of stelae in Romanesque and the list of the deceased better than you do.
If there are any procedural concerns, I will assist you.
You try to persuade her in a soft voice, but Oak Casket remains cold-faced and adamant.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The living caused the death of the deceased, and they build the stelae and create the archives to comfort themselves.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: They believe that by doing all this, they can atone for their sins and gain the forgiveness of the deceased.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Then they can bid the past farewell and continue to live in this world burden-free.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I refuse to participate in that.
Having said that, Oak Casket leans back in the interrogation chair, signaling the end of the conversation.
You've misunderstood me.
You sigh and patiently explain to Oak Casket.
We are not doing this for our own sake, nor to comfort ourselves... but to always remember the pain inflicted by this disaster...

The Romanesque Hall preserves the dignity of the deceased after death and resolves their final regrets. It is one of the most precious places in Syndicate, and also one of the important witnesses of this disaster.
That's why we want to rebuild it.
Oak Casket's attitude softens a bit. She stops refuting you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Yes... Where they are is the best place in the world... They are the most wonderful, peaceful, and reliable friends...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Alive, they were the heroes of Rustfire, the refugees of the Drifter Camp, and my good neighbors. After their death...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: They returned to Romanesque. I dressed them up the best I could and listened to the words they left in the last moments of life.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Answering their murmurs, I resolved many of their regrets... but there were always some I couldn't settle...
Can you tell me more about these regrets?
Oak Casket smiles.
She lifts her finger deftly, as if some invisible souls are lingering in the blank space of the interrogation room, lamenting their regrets to her.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: They take on many forms. A child complained he had never seen his parents. A man couldn't get over his hatred for the gang who murdered his family. An old woman said she hadn't had one good thing in life and that her life was pointless...
Is this related to that unresolvable regret?
Or... is this one of the reasons you refuse to help us?
In the silence, you can hardly hear her breathing.
After a while, she bends down slightly, leaning in closer, her unevenly colored eyes eerie in the dimness.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Answer me...
Her voice is icy, like a question from the dead.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Do you believe that... the future is always hopeful?
I believe in hope, just like I believe you're trying to help those who have lost hope.
You hold her gaze and tell her your choice.
Oak Casket sighs deeply, leaning back in the chair.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You're stubborn, aren't you?

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Then let me tell you a story.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Have you heard this story about a falcon and three pockets before?
No.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: This is a story told to me by a priest a long time ago. I've heard it dates back to before Nightfall.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: When people first came to this world, the golden falcon opened the way for them and gave them three pockets: One filled with wealth, one with power, and one with hope.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: The falcon told them the pocket of wealth could be found where merchants gathered and the pocket of power could be found in war.
I guess the pocket of hope was the hardest to find.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You're always smart at times like this.
Oak Casket smiles and continues while gazing at you.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: It's a pity that the priest... died before he finished telling this story.
Is that priest the one whose regret you couldn't resolve?
Oak Casket doesn't answer your question. Instead, she starts reciting that strange poem softly into the darkness.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You shall endure hardships and surpass all stelae in this world...

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: You shall meet the golden falcon, and the winged traveler will guide you...
She mutters emotionlessly, sounding more like she's mocking the poem than praying.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Those who have lost hope... can't even resolve their regrets.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Chief, where do you think we can find the pocket of hope?

options: I may not find it now.

choices.text: I may not find it now.

steps.content: I once found the pocket of hope with my own hands.
Perhaps the pockets of hope have become scarce in our world now, so much so that the regrets and the deceased you've ever encountered have never seen hope.
But the world has already started to change.
One day, the pocket of hope will appear before everyone's eyes.
Perhaps the pocket of hope doesn't exist in our world now.
But there are always people resisting this terrible world, striving to bring the pocket of hope back to this world.
Maybe we're indeed the unlucky ones. Maybe the world after Nightfall is just so terrible that hope no longer exists naturally.
But as long as we persist, one day, the pocket of hope will appear before everyone's eyes.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Do you think it is something that everyone can have?
Oak Casket is watching you, her eyes gleaming with interest.
Yes, as long as they're willing to persist.
I've been through countless hopeless situations... Yet I'm still standing here, instead of lying beneath a gravestone in Romanesque.
I believe that as long as you face it, one day you'll find a way to resolve even that unresolvable regret.
Oak Casket remains silent.
But from the other end of the shackles, you feel a tiny ripple of Mania.
It's impossible to fully convince her of a hopeful future within such a short conversation. But you want to at least show her the possibilities.
I have a suggestion, Oak Casket.
You take the spread-out file, remove the photos on it and put them in your pocket, then draft an application on the paper.
If I can't persuade you from the living's perspective, then we'll let the dead decide.
For the first time, some semblance of surprise emerges on Oak Casket's expressionless face.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Let the dead decide? How are you going to conduct this judgment when you can't even communicate with them?
I will sign a document permitting your return to the Drifter Camp for the reconstruction of Romanesque's stele garden. And I'll accompany you as your supervisor.
We'll resolve that regret together.
Upon hearing your proposal, her mismatched eyes radiate an almost hysterical brilliance.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: ...You're very bold, Chief.
You haven't seen her like this in a long time. The messenger of the dead who mocks the living recklessly.
If the dead approve of me... I hope you will too, and cooperate with us to rebuild West District.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Haha... After peeking into death, are you reaching to the message between life and death now too?
She looks at the application you handed over, a neat signature already printed after the supervisor's name. Oak Casket picks up the pen on the desk and signs her own name.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Very well, I accept your proposal.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: I will do my best to assist you, but you must touch the gravestones of Romanesque and listen to the whispers of the dead, and you can't leave even if it becomes too much for your mind to bear.

steps.speaker: Oak Casket
steps.content: Don't disappoint me.
As you exit the interrogation room, Oak Casket looks much more pleased than before.
You complete the application as quickly as possible, but Nightingale is still concerned.
You reassure her that Oak Casket has helped you many times before and that she'll do the same this time. Finally, Nightingale relents.
